0: Learning objective: use 0.8 times the baseline prediction loss plus 0.2 times mean softplus(negative_logit - positive_logit), pairing only positives and negatives already sampled at each valid training position. This adds direct ranking pressure without changing sampling or inference and may improve HR@10 on weaker categories. Preserve the baseline SASRec architecture, features, readout, optimizer and training settings; train one model per category across all four datasets.
1: Feature construction: add a deterministic prefix-repeat feature by multiplying each existing input item embedding by 1 + 0.1 * min(log1p(c), 2), where c counts earlier occurrences of that item in the visible causal prefix. Compute counts from supplied training history and available inference history only. This may distinguish repeated interests from incidental interactions without new embedding tables or a separate scorer. Keep positional embeddings, SASRec topology, readout, loss and optimizer fixed; retain one model per category.
2: Network architecture: scale each feed-forward residual branch by a fixed factor of 0.5 before adding it to the residual stream, leaving attention branches unchanged. Smaller feed-forward updates may reduce overfitting and preserve useful sequential representations in sparse categories. Retain the causal SASRec backbone, depth, heads, embedding design, features, scoring, readout, loss and optimizer. Mirror the residual scaling in the predictor writer and load one trained checkpoint per category.
3: Interest aggregation: replace each position's readout with 0.8 times its current causal encoder state plus 0.2 times an exponentially weighted mean of up to four preceding valid encoder states, using weights proportional to 2^(-lag). Fall back to the current state when no predecessor exists. Apply this causal readout during training and prediction. It may stabilize noisy last-item intent while retaining recency.
